status_reason: The UV-Vis transmission concept is blocked because black crude oil is opaque, and the MIR ATR alternative still depends on process conditions, fiber link length and validation data the client has not given.
answer: A UV-Vis transmission probe with a 10 mm path is not suitable for black crude oil, because the signal saturates in opaque samples. Test an MIR ATR probe on crude oil with known water content first, since a published petroleum application uses this method for water. The water range above 2.0 % and the fiber range still need checking before any in-line install.

inline.headline: Test MIR ATR on crude oil with known water content in the lab before any in-line install
inline.probe: ATR probe with ZrO2 tip sealed in a PEEK shaft
inline.install: In the pipe as a remote ATR probe, only after lab proof; process location and conditions are not yet known
inline.test_against: UV-ATR probe (UV-Vis) on the same samples
inline.not_final_because: The source water data only go to 2.0 % water while the enquiry asks for up to 3 %; no detection limit, link length or process conditions are given, and no validation data exist yet.

problems.text: Black crude oil is not a clear transparent liquid, and a 10 mm transmission path saturates when the sample is opaque, so the UV-Vis transmission concept will not work.
UV-Vis has low selectivity and strongly overlapping bands in real mixtures, so water would need chemometric models to be measured reliably.
The petroleum water data go only up to 2.0 % water, while the enquiry asks for up to 3 %; the range above 2.0 % is not covered by the sources.
The MIR water chart spans 4000-2000 cm-1, which is 2.5-5 µm; the PIR fiber transmits only 3-16 µm, so the band used must be checked to lie inside the fiber range.

methods.why: A published petroleum application uses an ATR probe to read water content, with absorbance rising as water goes from 0.1 to 2.0 %.
Transmission saturates on opaque oil; UV-ATR is the variant for opaque media, but UV-Vis has low selectivity, so it serves only as a comparison.
NIR is the most common online fiber-probe method and penetrates several millimetres, but its broad overlapping bands need chemometrics, and the sources give no water-in-petroleum example.
Raman signals are weak and are often masked by fluorescence in many organic compounds, so it is a later option only.

questions.q: Which water contents must be measured, is 3 % the upper limit, and what accuracy is required?
questions.why: The source data stop at 2.0 % water.

questions.q: What are the process temperature, pressure, flow and pipe location?
questions.why: The petroleum source gives no process conditions, so the probe and fiber choice cannot yet be confirmed.

questions.q: What fiber link length is needed between the probe and the spectrometer?
questions.why: No link length is given in the sources, and PIR fibers are the family that couples well to ATR probes.

questions.q: Do you have samples with independently measured water content for validation?
questions.why: A model needs validation on separate samples before any reading is trusted.

experiment.objective: Find out whether the MIR ATR spectrum of crude oil shows a water-dependent band over 0 to 3 % water.
steps: Prepare crude oil samples with known water contents covering 0 to 3 %, using the 0.1-2.0 % range from the source as a starting point.
Record MIR ATR spectra over 4000-2000 cm-1 through a PIR fiber link, and check that the band lies inside 3-16 µm.
Record UV-ATR spectra of the same samples as the comparison method.
Build a model on part of the samples and test it on separate samples with independent laboratory water analysis.
Compare MIR-only and UV-only results on the same validation samples to choose the method.
references: S02-13 p.13: water in petroleum, ATR probe and MIR absorbance example
S01 p.16: UV-Vis probe choice by optical density

pathway.key_features: Water-dependent absorbance in the 4000-2000 cm-1 region (the exact band is not named in the sources)
pathway.path_reason: The water signal and its validation with independent analyses must be proven in the lab first.

multispectral.why: MIR gives well-defined absorption peaks while NIR gives broad overlapping bands and penetrates deeper, so the two carry complementary information.
multispectral.test: On the same independent validation samples, the combined model must beat MIR ATR alone; if it does not, drop the combination.

assumptions: The MIR band that carries the water signal is not named in the sources and must be found from lab spectra.
Process temperature, pressure, flow and pipe location are unknown.
The client describes the sample both as a perfectly clear liquid and as black crude oil; black crude oil is taken as the true description.
